questions.q: In the sentence 'His sanguine forecast proved wrong when sales fell', the word 'sanguine' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Optimistic. Sanguine: hopeful and confident.

questions.q: He is not averse ____ working on weekends during the audit season.
questions.x: 'Averse' takes 'to'.

questions.q: The Secretary is a(n) ____ member of the board by virtue of his post.
questions.x: Ex officio: by virtue of office.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to 'ephemeral' as used in: 'The protest had only an ephemeral effect on policy.'
questions.x: Correct answer: Lasting. Ephemeral: short-lived.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
The officer asked me (that why I was late).
questions.x: Correct answer: why I was late. Reported questions drop 'that' and use statement order.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The audit was conducted / in accordance to / the prescribed standards.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'in accordance to'. The phrase is 'in accordance with'.

questions.q: She has been working in this office ____ 2019.
questions.x: 'Since' marks a point of time with the perfect continuous.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a coherent paragraph:
P: It was then refined by later scholars.
Q: The idea was first proposed in a short paper.
R: Today it forms the basis of the entire field.
S: At first, it attracted little attention.
questions.x: Correct answer: QSPR. Proposal → neglect → refinement → present status.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
She returned back / from the regional office / late last evening.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'She returned back'. 'Returned back' is redundant; 'returned' already means came back.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'Who prepared this report?'
o: By whom this report was prepared?
By whom has this report been prepared?
By whom was this report prepared?
questions.x: Past simple question in the passive keeps inversion: was + subject + past participle.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
(Despite of) the heavy rain, the match continued.
questions.x: 'Despite' takes no 'of'; 'in spite of' needs 'of'.

questions.q: The statement that wide roads 'invite more vehicles' implies that:
o: Wide roads reduce the number of cars
People stop using buses when roads are narrow
Road widening can create additional traffic that cancels its benefit
Congestion is caused only by pedestrians
questions.x: Answer: 'Road widening can create additional traffic that cancels its benefit'. This is the idea of induced demand. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A city built for cars measures success by how fast vehicles move. A city built for people asks a different question: how easily can a child walk to school, or an elderly person cross the road? Wide roads may speed traffic for a while, but they also invite more vehicles, and the congestion soon returns. Footpaths, safe crossings and frequent buses do not make headlines, yet they serve the majority who do not own cars.

questions.q: The author's main concern is that city planning should:
o: Focus mainly on increasing vehicle speed
Give priority to the needs of pedestrians and public transport users
questions.x: Answer: 'Give priority to the needs of pedestrians and public transport users'. The author favours a city 'built for people'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A city built for cars measures success by how fast vehicles move. A city built for people asks a different question: how easily can a child walk to school, or an elderly person cross the road? Wide roads may speed traffic for a while, but they also invite more vehicles, and the congestion soon returns. Footpaths, safe crossings and frequent buses do not make headlines, yet they serve the majority who do not own cars.

questions.q: Why does the author say footpaths and buses 'do not make headlines'?
o: They are disliked by the majority
They are banned in most cities
They are less visible than big projects though they serve most people
They are too expensive to build
questions.x: Answer: 'They are less visible than big projects though they serve most people'. The contrast is with headline-grabbing road projects. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A city built for cars measures success by how fast vehicles move. A city built for people asks a different question: how easily can a child walk to school, or an elderly person cross the road? Wide roads may speed traffic for a while, but they also invite more vehicles, and the congestion soon returns. Footpaths, safe crossings and frequent buses do not make headlines, yet they serve the majority who do not own cars.

questions.q: The 'two needs that pull in opposite directions' refer to:
o: Richer regions keeping their revenue and poorer regions needing support
questions.x: Answer: 'Richer regions keeping their revenue and poorer regions needing support'. This is explained in the second sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Federal systems must balance two needs that pull in opposite directions. Richer regions want to keep what they earn; poorer regions need support to provide basic services. If transfers are too small, inequality hardens; if they are too large and unconditional, they may weaken the incentive to raise revenue locally. The craft of fiscal federalism lies in designing transfers that both equalise and encourage effort.

questions.q: According to the passage, very large unconditional transfers may:
o: Reduce the incentive of regions to raise their own revenue
Make richer regions poorer than poorer ones
questions.x: Answer: 'Reduce the incentive of regions to raise their own revenue'. This is stated in the third sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Federal systems must balance two needs that pull in opposite directions. Richer regions want to keep what they earn; poorer regions need support to provide basic services. If transfers are too small, inequality hardens; if they are too large and unconditional, they may weaken the incentive to raise revenue locally. The craft of fiscal federalism lies in designing transfers that both equalise and encourage effort.

questions.q: Which title best suits the passage?
o: Why Rich Regions Should Pay Nothing
The Balancing Act of Fiscal Transfers
questions.x: Answer: 'The Balancing Act of Fiscal Transfers'. The passage is about designing transfers that balance competing goals. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Federal systems must balance two needs that pull in opposite directions. Richer regions want to keep what they earn; poorer regions need support to provide basic services. If transfers are too small, inequality hardens; if they are too large and unconditional, they may weaken the incentive to raise revenue locally. The craft of fiscal federalism lies in designing transfers that both equalise and encourage effort.

questions.q:
Which of the following leaders attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
1. Mahatma Gandhi
2. B. R. Ambedkar
3. Sarojini Naidu
4. Jawaharlal Nehru
How many of the above attended?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Nehru did not attend; Sarojini Naidu attended in her individual capacity.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. An iqta was an assignment of land revenue in return for service.
2. Iltutmish developed it into an administrative institution.
3. Iqta holders owned the land permanently and passed it to their heirs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Iqtas were transferable assignments, not ownership.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Bijolia movement:
1. It was a peasant movement in Mewar, Rajasthan.
2. Vijay Singh Pathik was associated with it.
3. It was the first movement led by Gandhi in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Gandhi's first movement in India was at Champaran (1917).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Komagata Maru episode of 1914 deepened anti-British feeling among Indians abroad.
Reason (R): Most of the ship's Indian passengers were refused entry into Canada, and several were killed in police firing at Budge Budge on their return.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The episode fed the Ghadar movement.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Mughal mansabdari system linked rank to military obligations.
Reason (R): Each mansabdar was required to maintain a specified number of horsemen (sawar) according to his rank.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Which of the following were outcomes of the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Provincial autonomy
2. Establishment of a Federal Court
3. Establishment of the Reserve Bank of India by this Act
4. Separation of Burma from India
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The RBI was created by the RBI Act, 1934, not by the 1935 Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Santhal rebellion (1855–56):
1. It was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu.
2. It was directed against zamindars, moneylenders and the colonial administration.
3. It led to the creation of a separate administrative unit, the Santhal Parganas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the demands of the early (Moderate) nationalists:
1. Expansion and reform of the legislative councils.
2. Holding the ICS examination simultaneously in India and England.
3. Complete independence from British rule from 1885 onwards.
Which of the above were demands of the Moderates?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Purna Swaraj was adopted only at the Lahore session of 1929.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Jain tradition:
1. Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara.
2. The Svetambara and Digambara sects differ, among other things, on the practice of wearing clothes by monks.
3. Jainism rejects the doctrine of karma.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Karma is central to Jain philosophy.

questions.q:
Consider the following about temple architecture:
1. The Nagara style is characterised by a curvilinear shikhara.
2. The Dravida style has a pyramidal vimana and large gopurams.
3. The Vesara style combines features of Nagara and Dravida.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY:
1. Since 2024 all citizens aged 70 and above are covered irrespective of income.
2. Coverage is ₹5 lakh per family per year.
3. It covers only outpatient consultations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It covers secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Union Budget 2025-26 announced coverage of gig and platform workers under PM-JAY.
Reason (R): Gig workers were to be registered on the e-Shram portal and given identity cards.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both were announced together; registration is a separate step, not the cause of health coverage.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Digital Personal Data Protection framework:
1. The Act was passed in 2023.
2. It establishes the Data Protection Board of India.
3. Its rules were notified in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's technology missions:
1. The National Quantum Mission runs from 2023-24 to 2030-31.
2. The IndiaAI Mission includes building shared GPU compute capacity.
3. India co-chaired the AI Action Summit in Paris in February 2025 and was chosen to host the next summit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The next summit, the AI Impact Summit, was planned in New Delhi in 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following about women's labour force participation in India:
1. Female labour force participation rose sharply between 2017-18 and 2023-24 according to PLFS.
2. Much of the increase came from rural self-employment.
3. The increase was driven mainly by formal salaried jobs in cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Self-employment, much of it unpaid family work in rural areas, drove most of the rise.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A consumption-based Gini index usually shows lower inequality than an income-based one.
Reason (R): Richer households save a larger share of their income than poorer ones.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Savings rise with income, so consumption is more evenly spread than income.

questions.q:
Consider the following about international summits in 2025:
1. The BRICS summit was hosted by Brazil at Rio de Janeiro.
2. The SCO summit was held at Tianjin, China.
3. The G20 Leaders' Summit was held for the first time in Africa, at Johannesburg.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three took place in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the NATO summit in The Hague (June 2025):
1. Allies agreed to a target of 5% of GDP on defence and security-related spending by 2035.
2. The target includes 3.5% for core defence.
3. India attended as a NATO member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India is not a NATO member.

questions.q:
Consider the following naval developments of 2025:
1. INS Tamal, built in Russia, was commissioned in 2025 as the last major warship imported by India.
2. INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri, Project 17A frigates, were commissioned together.
3. INS Vikrant was commissioned in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
INS Vikrant was commissioned in September 2022.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): 'Heart Lamp' was the first Kannada work to win the International Booker Prize.
Reason (R): The International Booker Prize honours a work of fiction translated into English, sharing the prize between author and translator.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R describes the prize, not why this was the first Kannada winner.

questions.q:
Consider the following monetary policy actions of the RBI in June 2025:
1. The repo rate was cut by 50 basis points.
2. The cash reserve ratio was to be cut by 100 basis points to 3% in tranches.
3. The policy stance was changed from 'neutral' to 'withdrawal of accommodation'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The stance was changed from 'accommodative' to 'neutral'.

questions.q:
Consider the following about tribunals:
1. Article 323A provides for administrative tribunals for public servants.
2. Articles 323A and 323B were inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
3. Tribunals under Article 323B can be set up only by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Under Article 323B, both Parliament and State legislatures can set up tribunals.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Council of Ministers:
1. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
2. A person who is not a Member of Parliament can be a minister for up to six months.
3. The Council is collectively responsible to both Houses of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha only.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Inter-State Council:
1. It is provided under Article 263.
2. It was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission.
3. Its recommendations are binding on States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is advisory.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Fundamental Rights:
1. Rights under Articles 15, 16 and 19 are available only to citizens.
2. Article 21 protects both citizens and non-citizens.
3. All Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a national emergency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an emergency (44th Amendment).

questions.q:
Match the Directive Principle with its subject:
Article:
A. Article 40
B. Article 44
C. Article 48A
D. Article 50
Subject:
1. Protection of environment, forests and wildlife
2. Separation of judiciary from executive
3. Organisation of village panchayats
4. Uniform civil code
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Article 40) → 3 (Organisation of village panchayats); B (Article 44) → 4 (Uniform civil code); C (Article 48A) → 1 (Protection of environment, forests and wildlife); D (Article 50) → 2 (Separation of judiciary from executive).
Standard DPSP mapping.

questions.q:
Which of the following are special powers of the Rajya Sabha?
1. It can authorise the creation of new All-India Services.
2. It alone can move a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
3. It can reject a Money Bill.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is incorrect.
No-confidence motions lie only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes to a Money Bill within 14 days.

questions.q: If both the President and the Vice-President are unavailable, who discharges the functions of the President?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Justice of India (or in absence, the senior-most Supreme Court judge)
questions.x: Correct answer: The Chief Justice of India (or in absence, the senior-most Supreme Court judge). Under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court can review its own judgments.
Reason (R): Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its judgments or orders.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following provisions is borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: The scheme of the federal structure with Union, State and Concurrent lists of legislative subjects
questions.x: A large part of the administrative and federal framework came from the 1935 Act.

questions.q:
Consider the following Fundamental Duties under Article 51A:
1. To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
2. To safeguard public property and abjure violence.
3. To vote in every election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Voting is not listed as a Fundamental Duty.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The CAG is called the guardian of the public purse.
Reason (R): The CAG audits receipts and expenditure of the Union and the States to ensure money is spent as authorised.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Match the body with its constitutional basis:
Body:
A. Finance Commission
B. Union Public Service Commission
C. GST Council
D. National Commission for Backward Classes
Article:
1. Article 280
2. Article 315
3. Article 338B
4. Article 279A
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Finance Commission) → 1 (Article 280); B (Union Public Service Commission) → 2 (Article 315); C (GST Council) → 4 (Article 279A); D (National Commission for Backward Classes) → 3 (Article 338B).
Key constitutional bodies.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker decides questions of disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review.
2. The Speaker presides over joint sittings.
3. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct (Kihoto Hollohan; Article 118; Article 94).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023):
1. It reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
2. Reservation takes effect after delimitation based on the first census after its commencement.
3. It reserves one-third of seats in the Rajya Sabha for women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils are not covered.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹2,91,250 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹2,33,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (2,91,250 / 2,33,000) × 100 = 125.
Prices have risen 25% over the base year.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Minimum Support Prices:
1. They are announced on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.
2. Sugarcane has a Fair and Remunerative Price instead of an MSP.
3. MSP is legally guaranteed for all crops in all markets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
There is no statutory guarantee of MSP purchase for all crops.

questions.q: Which of the following combinations of RBI actions is the most contractionary?
o: Raise repo rate and sell government securities
Cut repo rate and raise SLR
Raise SDF rate and buy foreign currency
Cut CRR and buy government securities
questions.x: Correct answer: Raise repo rate and sell government securities. Both a repo hike and OMO sales tighten liquidity.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the FRBM framework:
1. The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003.
2. The N. K. Singh Committee recommended using debt-to-GDP as the primary anchor.
3. The FRBM Act prohibits the Centre from borrowing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Act sets deficit and debt targets; it does not prohibit borrowing.

questions.q:
Consider the following about audit evidence and procedures:
1. Vouching examines documentary evidence supporting entries in the books.
2. Verification establishes the existence, ownership and valuation of assets and liabilities.
3. Test checking means examining every transaction in detail.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Test checking examines a representative sample.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): After paying a claim for a damaged car, the insurer can sue the negligent third party.
Reason (R): Under subrogation, the insurer steps into the shoes of the insured after indemnifying him.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Provisions are a charge against profit, while reserves are an appropriation of profit.
2. A reserve can be created even when the business incurs a loss for the year.
3. Provision for doubtful debts is an application of conservatism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Reserves are appropriations of profit and cannot be created out of a loss.

questions.q: A firm has current assets of ₹4,00,000, which include inventory of ₹1,00,000 and prepaid expenses of ₹20,000. Its current liabilities are ₹2,00,000. What is its quick ratio?
Opening inventory is ₹90,000, closing inventory is ₹90,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹3,60,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (90,000 + 90,000) / 2 = ₹90,000.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 3,60,000 / 90,000 = 4 times.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹60,000; Purchases ₹2,10,000; Purchase returns ₹3,000; Carriage inwards ₹1,000; Sales ₹2,50,500; Sales returns ₹4,000; Closing stock ₹35,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 60,000 + 2,10,000 − 3,000 + 1,000 − 35,000 = ₹2,33,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 2,50,500 − 4,000 − 2,33,000 = ₹13,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Office furniture is purchased for ₹4,05,000 and ₹9,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 8 years with a residual value of ₹12,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (4,05,000 + 9,000 − 12,000) / 8 = 4,02,000 / 8 = ₹50,250 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: A machine bought for ₹2,00,000 is depreciated at 10% p.a. on WDV. At the end of year 2 it is sold for ₹1,50,000. The profit or loss on sale is:

A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹3,85,000 and at the end ₹4,72,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹50,000 and withdrew ₹2,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 4,72,500 + 2,500 − 50,000 − 3,85,000 = ₹40,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: Debtors are ₹1,05,000. Bad debts to be written off ₹5,000; provision for doubtful debts at 5%; provision for discount at 2%. The net debtors shown in the balance sheet are:
A bill of exchange drawn on 15 January for 2 months after date (no holiday issues) matures on:
questions.x: 15 March + 3 days of grace = 18 March.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a change brought by the Labour Codes?
o: Making employment exchanges compulsory for all recruitment
questions.x: Employment exchanges were renamed Career Centres; the Codes do not make them compulsory for every recruitment.

questions.q: A State law prohibits workers from forming any association. Which constitutional provision is most directly violated?
questions.x: Article 19(1)(c) guarantees the right to form associations or unions, subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(4).

questions.q:
With reference to the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, consider the following:
1. On commencement of the Act, every bonded debt stood extinguished.
2. Vigilance Committees are constituted at district and sub-divisional levels.
3. Offences under the Act are triable by Executive Magistrates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are provisions of the 1976 Act (Sections 6, 13, 21).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The IR Code requires an employer to contribute fifteen days' wages per retrenched worker to a Worker Re-skilling Fund.
Reason (R): The fund is meant to help retrenched workers acquire new skills for re-employment.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The Fund (Section 83) credits the amount to the worker within 45 days to support re-skilling.

questions.q: An establishment deducts 4% of a worker's wages as a fine for late attendance during a month. Under the Code on Wages, the deduction is:
o: Lawful, because late attendance is misconduct
Unlawful only if the worker is a woman
Unlawful, because a fine cannot exceed 3% of wages for the wage period
questions.x: Correct answer: Unlawful, because a fine cannot exceed 3% of wages for the wage period. Fines are capped at 3% of wages in the wage period.

questions.q: A unit pays a worker ₹15,000 as basic + DA, ₹9,000 as HRA, ₹3,000 as conveyance and ₹3,000 as overtime for the month (total ₹30,000). For computing 'wages' under the Code on Wages, the amount is:
o: ₹18,000, after adding back the excess over 50%
₹15,000, since excluded items (₹15,000) do not exceed half of ₹30,000
questions.x: Excluded components (HRA ₹9,000 + conveyance ₹3,000 + overtime ₹3,000) = ₹15,000, which is exactly 50% of total remuneration. The add-back applies only to the amount exceeding one-half, so nothing is added; wages = ₹15,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Code on Wages prohibits discrimination on the ground of gender in recruitment for the same work.
Reason (R): The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976, now subsumed in the Code, applied only to wages and not to recruitment.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is correct. R is false — the Equal Remuneration Act also prohibited discrimination in recruitment (Section 5).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the early trade union movement in India:
1. The Madras Labour Union (1918) was organised by B. P. Wadia.
2. AITUC was founded in 1920 with Lala Lajpat Rai as its first president.
3. The Trade Unions Act was enacted in 1926 after the Buckingham Mill dispute had exposed unions to civil liability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q: Which of the following is a precondition for an employer's lock-out to be lawful under the IR Code?
o: Notice within sixty days before the lock-out, and no lock-out within fourteen days of the notice
Permission of the Industrial Tribunal in every case
A prior strike by the workers
questions.x: Correct answer: Notice within sixty days before the lock-out, and no lock-out within fourteen days of the notice. Lock-out restrictions mirror strike restrictions under Section 62(2).

questions.q: Under the IR Code, a worker continuously laid off for 50 days in a year in a 150-worker factory is offered retrenchment. Which statement best describes the legal position?
o: Retrenchment is barred while lay-off lasts
The worker becomes a permanent employee by operation of law
The employer may retrench after the first 45 days by following retrenchment conditions; lay-off compensation already paid can be set off
questions.x: Section 67 permits retrenchment after 45 days of lay-off in a 12-month period, with set-off of lay-off compensation paid in the preceding 12 months.

questions.q: A temporary employee who has worked for years seeks regularisation by court order despite irregular initial appointment. The Constitution Bench precedent most directly against automatic regularisation is:
o: State of Punjab v. Jagjit Singh (2016)
Secretary, State of Karnataka v. Umadevi (2006)
questions.x: Umadevi held that regularisation cannot be claimed as of right, though Jagjit Singh later secured equal pay for equal work for temporaries.

questions.q:
Which of the following are entitlements of an inter-State migrant worker under the OSH Code?
1. An annual lump-sum amount for a to-and-fro journey to the native place
2. Coverage even if the worker migrated on his or her own, not through a contractor
3. A toll-free helpline and registration in a national database
4. Guaranteed permanent employment at the destination
How many of the above are provided?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The first three are provided; permanent employment is not guaranteed.

questions.q:
Consider the following perspectives on industrial relations:
1. The unitary view treats conflict as abnormal and unions as unnecessary.
2. The pluralist view accepts conflict as natural and seeks to institutionalise it through bargaining.
3. The Marxist view sees industrial conflict as rooted in the wider class structure of society.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are standard characterisations (Fox; Flanders; Hyman).

questions.q:
Consider the following measures in labour statistics:
1. Worker Population Ratio is employed persons as a share of total population.
2. Unemployment Rate is unemployed persons as a share of the labour force.
3. Labour Force Participation Rate excludes persons seeking work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
LFPR includes both the employed and those seeking/available for work.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (2025):
1. It was earlier known as the Employment Linked Incentive scheme.
2. Its benefits are linked to employment in establishments registered with EPFO.
3. It provides an incentive to first-time employees and to employers for additional hiring.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; it covers jobs created from August 2025 to July 2027.

questions.q:
Which of the following are among the nine branches of social security in ILO Convention No. 102?
1. Employment injury benefit
2. Family benefit
3. Housing benefit
4. Invalidity benefit
How many of the above are among them?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Housing is not among the nine branches.

questions.q:
Consider the following under the Code on Social Security, 2020:
1. ESI coverage can be made mandatory for an establishment with even one employee in a hazardous occupation.
2. Aggregators must contribute 1–2% of annual turnover, subject to a cap of 5% of payments to gig and platform workers.
3. Gig workers are deemed to be employees of the aggregator.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Code does not make gig workers employees.

questions.q: An ESI-covered worker earns ₹20,000 a month. The employer and employee contributions for the month are respectively:
questions.x: Correct answer: ₹650 and ₹150. Employer 3.25% = ₹650; employee 0.75% = ₹150 (rates since July 2019).

questions.q:
Consider the following about PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM):
1. The Central Government makes a matching contribution.
2. LIC is the fund manager.
3. Members of EPFO, ESIC or NPS can also join it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Workers already covered under EPF, ESI or NPS are excluded.

questions.q:
Consider the following about EPFO's digital initiatives:
1. UAN was launched in 2014.
2. The Centralised Pension Payment System lets pensioners receive pension in any bank account.
3. Aadhaar seeding with UAN is optional for filing ECR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Aadhaar seeding is mandatory for ECR filing.

questions.q: An employee retires after 29 years and 3 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹34,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
3 months is not more than six months, so it is ignored → 29 years.
= 15/26 × 34,000 × 29 = ₹5,68,846 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Central Board of Trustees (EPF):
1. It is chaired by the Union Minister for Labour and Employment.
2. It has equal representation of employers and employees.
3. It fixes the EPF interest rate without any role for the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The rate recommended by the CBT is notified after concurrence of the Ministry of Finance.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the e-Shram portal:
1. Unorganised workers aged 16 to 59 can register on it.
2. Registered workers get a universal account number on an e-Shram card.
3. Members of EPFO and ESIC are encouraged to register on it as unorganised workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Workers covered by EPFO or ESIC are not eligible to register as unorganised workers.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹19,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹6,500 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 10%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 6,500) = ₹7,000.
Salary for computation = min(19,500, 7,000) = ₹7,000.
Annual bonus = 7,000 × 12 × 10% = ₹8,400. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: An employee drawing monthly wages of ₹39,000 dies in an accident arising out of and in the course of employment. The relevant factor applicable to the deceased is 104.31. Taking the wage ceiling of ₹15,000 notified for computing compensation, the compensation payable is:
questions.x:
For death: 50% of monthly wages × relevant factor, subject to a minimum of ₹1,20,000.
Wages for computation = min(39,000, 15,000) = 15,000.
0.5 × 15,000 × 104.31 = ₹7,82,325 → payable ₹7,82,325.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY:
1. Since October 2024, all senior citizens aged 70 and above are eligible irrespective of income.
2. It provides cashless secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
3. It is implemented by ESIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is implemented by the National Health Authority.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Baking powder makes cakes soft and spongy.
Reason (R): On heating, the sodium hydrogen carbonate in it releases carbon dioxide.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The gas bubbles make the batter rise.

questions.q:
Consider the following about spreadsheet functions:
1. VLOOKUP searches for a value in the first column of a range and returns a value from another column of the same row.
2. In a cell reference such as $A1, the column stays fixed when the formula is copied.
3. =SUM(A1:A3) adds only cells A1 and A3.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A1:A3 is a range covering A1, A2 and A3.

questions.q: What is the binary equivalent of the decimal number 45?
The hexadecimal number 2F equals which decimal number?

Consider the following about iodine and the thyroid:
1. Iodine deficiency can cause goitre.
2. Thyroxine regulates the basal metabolic rate.
3. Iodised salt is potassium chloride with added iodine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Iodised salt is common salt (sodium chloride) fortified with potassium iodate or iodide.

questions.q:
Consider the following about transformers:
1. They work on the principle of mutual induction.
2. They can step up or step down alternating voltage.
3. They work equally well on steady direct current.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A steady DC produces no changing flux, so no voltage is induced in the secondary.

questions.q:
Consider the following about cyber-security institutions in India:
1. CERT-In is the national agency for responding to cyber security incidents.
2. CERT-In directions of 2022 require reporting of specified incidents within six hours.
3. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The national cybercrime helpline is 1930.

questions.q:
Consider the following about HTTPS:
1. It encrypts data between the browser and the website using TLS.
2. It guarantees that the website itself is honest and safe to use.
3. Its default port is 443.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
HTTPS secures the connection, not the intentions of the site owner; phishing sites can use HTTPS too.

questions.q:
Consider the following about open-source software:
1. Its source code is available for anyone to study and modify, subject to its licence.
2. Open-source software must always be free of cost.
3. Linux and LibreOffice are examples of open-source software.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
'Free' in open source refers to freedom; some open-source software is sold with support.

questions.q:
Consider the following about quantum computing:
1. A qubit can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1.
2. Entanglement links qubits so that their states are correlated.
3. Large quantum computers could break widely used public-key schemes such as RSA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
This is why post-quantum cryptography is being standardised.

questions.q: Astronomers detect many exoplanets because the star's brightness dips slightly at regular intervals. This is called:
questions.x: A planet crossing the stellar disc blocks a small fraction of its light.

questions.q:
Consider the following about C4 plants:
1. Maize and sugarcane are C4 plants.
2. They are more efficient than C3 plants in hot and bright conditions.
3. They have no photorespiration at all and need no carbon dioxide.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
C4 plants still need CO₂; they concentrate it around RuBisCO, which greatly reduces photorespiration.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 7, 39, 12, 34, 17, 29, 22, ?
questions.x: Two interleaved series: odd positions 7, 12, 17, 22 (+5); even positions 39, 34, 29 (−5). The 8th term belongs to the even series: 29 − 5 = 24.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill an overhead tank in 15 hours and 35 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 21 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(15, 35, 21) = 105 units.
Rates: +7, +3, −5 units/hour → net 5 units/hour.
Time = 105 / 5 = 21 hours.

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹50,000. B joins after 7 months with ₹50,000, and C joins after 6 months with ₹45,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹1,56,800, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 50,000×12, B: 50,000×5, C: 45,000×6 → 60 : 25 : 27.
B's share = 25/112 × 1,56,800 = ₹35,000.

questions.q: A train 280 m long running at 72 km/h crosses a platform in 38 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. Distance covered in 38 s = 760 m = train + platform.
Platform = 760 − 280 = 480 m.

questions.q: A bag has 5 white and 7 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(7,2)/C(12,2) = 21/66.
Required = 1 − 7/22 = 15/22.

questions.q: Ravi can paint a hall in 15 days and Kiran in 60 days. They start together, but Ravi leaves after 9 days. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.x:
Work done together in 9 days = 9 × (1/15 + 1/60) = 9/12 = 3/4.
Remaining = 1/4, done by Kiran alone in 1/4 × 60 = 15 days.
Total = 9 + 15 = 24 days.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 20 years. In how many years will it become 4 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 20 years, i.e. rate = 100/20 = 5% p.a.
To become 4 times, interest must be 3 × principal.
Time = (3 × 100) / 5 = 60 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: On which day of the week did 11 December 1843 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1842: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 200 years → 3; remaining 42 years have 10 leap + 32 ordinary → 10×2 + 32 = 52 → 3 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1843 up to 11 December = 345 → 2 odd day(s).
Total = 3 + 3 + 2 = 8 → 1 → Monday.

questions.q: At what time between 10 and 11 o'clock will the hands of a clock point in opposite directions (be in a straight line but opposite)?
questions.x:
At 10:00 the minute hand is 50 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To be opposite it must gain 50 − 30 = 20 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 20 × 60/55 = 240/11 minutes = 21 9/11 minutes past 10.

questions.q: In a row, Sonal is 18th from the left and Vikram is 15th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Sonal becomes 26th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Sonal occupies Vikram's old place, which is 15th from the right and now 26th from the left.
Total = 26 + 15 − 1 = 40.

questions.q: The average of 9 observations is 43. The average of the first 5 is 49 and that of the last 5 is 46. The 5th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 9 = 9 × 43 = 387.
First 5 + last 5 = 5×49 + 5×46 = 475; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 475 − 387 = 88.

questions.q: ₹8,000 is invested for 1 year at 12% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 12/2 = 6%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 8,000 × (1 + 6/100)² = ₹8,988.80.
CI = ₹988.80 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹960).

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word 'BANKING' be arranged so that all the vowels always come together?
questions.x:
Vowels: A, I; consonants: B, N, K, N, G.
Treat the vowels as one block → 6 units → 360 arrangements (N appears 2 times).
Vowels inside the block: 2 ways (all letters are distinct).
Total = 360 × 2 = 720.

questions.q: A, B and C can complete a contract alone in 29, 9 and 30 days respectively. Working together they finish it and receive ₹93,400. If payment is in proportion to the work done, C's share is:
questions.x:
Daily work rates are 1/29 : 1/9 : 1/30 = 90 : 290 : 87 (LCM 2610).
Working together, work done is in the same ratio, so C gets 87/467 × 93,400 = ₹17,400.

questions.q:
Members enrolled in a district (thousand) — 2019: 265  |  2020: 315  |  2021: 370  |  2022: 430  |  2023: 430.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2020: 18.87%; 2021: 17.46%; 2022: 16.22%; 2023: 0%.
Highest growth: 2020 (18.87%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.
